# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009 of 22 June 2009, which amends Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 (REACH) -- the consolidated list of restricted substances, mixtures, and articles -- folding in prior Directive 76/769/EEC amendments (PFOS, arsenic compounds, mercury measuring devices, several solvents), deleting superfluous entries, and clarifying grandfather clauses and exemptions across many existing entries.

FACT: Done at Brussels, 22 June 2009. *Source: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009, EUR-Lex CELEX 32009R0552. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

*Analytical inference:* this is a consolidating and clarifying amendment to an already-large restriction list (Annex XVII), not a single new prohibition; this brief focuses on the recitals' own account of what changed and the one entry (chrysotile diaphragms) whose reporting deadline is squarely within this item's required slots.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: substances, mixtures or articles may not be manufactured, placed on the market or used unless they comply with the conditions of any restrictions laid down in their regard in Annex XVII. *Source: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009, recital 2. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Article 67 of Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 makes Annex XVII directly binding on any manufacturer, importer, distributor, or user of a restricted substance, mixture, or article; whether a specific workspace's own goods fall within a specific Annex XVII entry (this Regulation amends the entries for PFOS, arsenic compounds, mercury measuring devices, asbestos, PBDE flame retardants, nonylphenol, and several deleted/superseded entries) is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: However, Member States may exempt the placing on the market and use of diaphragms containing chrysotile (point (f)) for existing electrolysis installations until they reach the end of their service life, or until suitable asbestos-free substitutes become available, whichever is the sooner. *Source: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009, Annex (asbestos entry). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

FACT: By 1 June 2011 Member States making use of this exemption shall provide a report to the Commission on the availability of asbestos free substitutes for electrolysis installations *Source: same Annex entry. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

*Operational implication:* the 1 June 2011 reporting deadline itself is already historical relative to the current date, but the underlying exemption it monitors (chrysotile-containing diaphragms in existing electrolysis installations) remains conditional on the installation not yet reaching end of service life or asbestos-free substitutes not yet being available; a workspace with EU chlor-alkali electrolysis exposure should confirm current status directly rather than relying on this 2009-era snapshot.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States. *Source: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009, Article 2. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

*Legal Confirmation Required:* as an EU Regulation, this instrument (and the Annex XVII it amends) is directly applicable without national transposition, binding on any manufacturer, importer, distributor, or downstream user of a listed substance, mixture, or article; it does not itself create a duty on a carrier or freight forwarder as such, though a freight forwarder handling restricted goods should confirm its principal's own compliance.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: The substances carbon tetrachloride and 1,1,1-trichloroethane are severely restricted under Regulation (EC) No 2037/2000 *Source: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009, recital 10. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

FACT: Restrictions on carbon tetrachloride and 1,1,1-trichloroethane in Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) 1907/2006 are therefore superfluous and should be deleted. *Source: same recital. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

FACT: Since mercury in batteries is regulated under Directive 2006/66/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 6 September 2006 on batteries and accumulators and waste batteries and accumulators ( 11 ) , the provisions on mercury in batteries currently contained in Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 are superfluous and should therefore be deleted. *Source: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009, recital 11. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

*Analytical inference:* both deletions reflect the same drafting principle -- Annex XVII does not duplicate a restriction already fully covered by another directly applicable EU instrument (Regulation (EC) No 2037/2000 for ozone-depleting solvents, Directive 2006/66/EC for battery mercury).

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

1. Chrysotile-diaphragm exemption report (event date 1 June 2011). FACT: By 1 June 2011 Member States making use of this exemption shall provide a report to the Commission on the availability of asbestos free substitutes for electrolysis installations *Source: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009, Annex (asbestos entry, the fuller sentence this event is drawn from). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

*Operational implication:* the export's own forward-event record for this item names this same 1 June 2011 reporting deadline; the fuller sentence quoted above states that following receipt of these reports, the Commission is to request the Agency to prepare a dossier with a view to prohibiting the placing on the market of chrysotile-containing diaphragms outright, so this reporting deadline is itself a precursor to a possible future prohibition, not a self-contained requirement.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does the PFOS restriction apply to PFOS-containing products already on the market before this Regulation?**

FACT: It should be made clear that the restriction incorporated in Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 concerning perfluorooctane sulfonates does not apply to products which were already in use in the Community when the restriction entered into force. *Source: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009, recital 20. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

*Legal Confirmation Required:* no; the restriction is grandfathered for products already in use in the Community when the restriction entered into force.

**Q2: Does the mercury-measuring-device restriction require withdrawal of devices already in service?**

FACT: the restrictions incorporated in Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 on the marketing of certain measuring devices containing mercury do not apply to devices already in use in the Community at the time of entry into force of the restriction. *Source: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009, recital 17. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

*Legal Confirmation Required:* no; the same grandfather principle applies -- devices already in use in the Community at the time of entry into force are not covered.

**Q3: Do the flame-retardant (PBDE) restrictions apply to second-hand aeroplanes or vehicles already in service?**

FACT: it should be provided that the restrictions do not apply to articles already in use at the date from which the restriction was to apply as those substances were incorporated in articles which have a long lifecycle and are sold on the second hand market, such as aeroplanes and vehicles. *Source: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009, recital 18. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

*Legal Confirmation Required:* no; articles already in use at the date from which the restriction was to apply are grandfathered, specifically because these substances were incorporated into long-lifecycle, second-hand-market goods such as aeroplanes and vehicles.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. General Annex XVII authorisation-to-use mechanism.** FACT: substances, mixtures or articles may not be manufactured, placed on the market or used unless they comply with the conditions of any restrictions laid down in their regard in Annex XVII. *Source: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009, recital 2. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

**2. PFOS grandfather clause.** FACT: It should be made clear that the restriction incorporated in Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 concerning perfluorooctane sulfonates does not apply to products which were already in use in the Community when the restriction entered into force. *Source: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009, recital 20. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

**3. Chrysotile-diaphragm exemption and reporting deadline.** FACT: However, Member States may exempt the placing on the market and use of diaphragms containing chrysotile (point (f)) for existing electrolysis installations until they reach the end of their service life, or until suitable asbestos-free substitutes become available, whichever is the sooner. *Source: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009, Annex (asbestos entry). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

FACT: By 1 June 2011 Member States making use of this exemption shall provide a report to the Commission on the availability of asbestos free substitutes for electrolysis installations *Source: same Annex entry. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

**4. Cross-entry export/transfer exemption (Entries 1 to 58).** FACT: for substances which have been incorporated in Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 as a consequence of restrictions adopted in the framework of Directive 76/769/EEC (Entries 1 to 58), the restrictions do not apply to storage, keeping, treatment, filling into containers, or transfer from one container to another of the substances for export, unless the manufacture of the substances is prohibited. *Source: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009, recital 15. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

**5. Mercury-measuring-device grandfather clause.** FACT: the restrictions incorporated in Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 on the marketing of certain measuring devices containing mercury do not apply to devices already in use in the Community at the time of entry into force of the restriction. *Source: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009, recital 17. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

**6. PBDE flame-retardant grandfather clause.** FACT: it should be provided that the restrictions do not apply to articles already in use at the date from which the restriction was to apply as those substances were incorporated in articles which have a long lifecycle and are sold on the second hand market, such as aeroplanes and vehicles. *Source: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009, recital 18. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

**7. Nonylphenol ethoxylate national-authorisation preservation.** FACT: It should be made clear in the restriction on nonylphenol and nonylphenol ethoxylate that the validity of existing national authorisations for pesticides and biocidal products containing nonylphenol ethoxylate as co-formulant should not be affected *Source: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009, recital 19. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

**8. Deletion of the carbon tetrachloride / 1,1,1-trichloroethane restrictions as superfluous.** FACT: Restrictions on carbon tetrachloride and 1,1,1-trichloroethane in Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) 1907/2006 are therefore superfluous and should be deleted. *Source: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009, recital 10. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

**9. Deletion of the mercury-in-batteries provision as superfluous.** FACT: Since mercury in batteries is regulated under Directive 2006/66/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 6 September 2006 on batteries and accumulators and waste batteries and accumulators ( 11 ) , the provisions on mercury in batteries currently contained in Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 are superfluous and should therefore be deleted. *Source: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009, recital 11. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

**10. Entry into force.** FACT: This Regulation shall enter into force on the day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union *Source: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009, Article 2. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

**11. Binding and directly applicable in all Member States.** FACT: This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States. *Source: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009, Article 2. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 2 of this Regulation beyond the single 1 June 2011 reporting deadline already stated as substantive requirement 3; the grandfather clauses (obligations 2, 5, 6) are one-time cutoffs tied to each restriction's own entry-into-force date, not a multi-year schedule. Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED via the FACT claim declaring this section for the chrysotile-diaphragm exemption above, whose source_span contains the unnegated word "exempt" ("Member States may exempt the placing on the market and use of diaphragms containing chrysotile..."). Scope limits: CAPTURED via the FACT claim declaring this section for the PFOS grandfather clause above, whose source_span contains the unnegated phrase "does not apply" ("...does not apply to products which were already in use in the Community when the restriction entered into force.").

Obligations surveyed: 11; workspace-adjacent: 11; extracted as FACT: 11.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

FACT: However, Member States may exempt the placing on the market and use of diaphragms containing chrysotile (point (f)) for existing electrolysis installations until they reach the end of their service life, or until suitable asbestos-free substitutes become available, whichever is the sooner. *Source: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009, Annex (asbestos entry). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

FACT: it should be provided that the restrictions do not apply to articles already in use at the date from which the restriction was to apply as those substances were incorporated in articles which have a long lifecycle and are sold on the second hand market, such as aeroplanes and vehicles. *Source: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009, recital 18. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

*Operational implication:* the two product categories most likely to intersect a freight-forwarding workspace's own cargo are long-lifecycle second-hand goods (aeroplanes, vehicles) carrying legacy PBDE flame retardants, and any chlor-alkali-adjacent chemical shipments touching chrysotile-diaphragm electrolysis installations; both categories carry a grandfather clause rather than an outright prohibition on already-in-service goods.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Operational implication:* a workspace with EU chlor-alkali electrolysis exposure should confirm, directly with the operator or the Commission's own published information, whether the chrysotile-diaphragm exemption (Section 8, obligation 3) remains active for a specific installation, since this brief's own corpus is a 2009-era snapshot and the exemption is conditioned on service life and substitute availability that changes over time.

FACT: It should be made clear that the restriction incorporated in Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 concerning perfluorooctane sulfonates does not apply to products which were already in use in the Community when the restriction entered into force. *Source: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009, recital 20. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009R0552

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the export/transfer exemption (Entries 1 to 58) is itself conditional -- it does not apply where the manufacture of the substance is prohibited outright, rather than merely restricted in use.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 22 June 2009: Commission Regulation (EC) No 552/2009 adopted at Brussels.
- 26 June 2009: Published in the Official Journal of the European Union (Series L 164/7).
- 1 June 2011: Deadline for Member States using the chrysotile-diaphragm exemption to report to the Commission on asbestos-free substitute availability and the envisaged date of the end of the exemption.

# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks The Vehicle Excise Duty (Reduced Pollution) (Amendment) Regulations 2000 (S.I. 2000/3274), a UK statutory instrument amending the Vehicle Excise Duty (Reduced Pollution) Regulations 1998. It exists to give a freight forwarder or motor-carrier operator with vehicles registered in the workspace's GB fleet a single record of the particulate-emission thresholds relevant to the reduced-pollution Vehicle Excise Duty (VED) rate.

FACT: "These Regulations amend the Vehicle Excise Duty (Reduced Pollution) Regulations 1998." *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2000/3274*

*Operational implication:* A workspace operating GB-registered goods vehicles that hold, or are seeking, a reduced pollution certificate under the 1998 Regulations should read this 2000 amendment as changing the particulate-emission figures a vehicle must meet under that certificate scheme, not as a freestanding new duty.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-13: this record-grade item's captured source is a completed 2000 amendment instrument that has been in force since 5th January 2001; the captured text states no pending or future action item.*

FACT: "in exercise of the powers conferred by sections 57 and 61B of the Vehicle Excise and Registration Act 1994" *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2000/3274*

# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Decision 2013/162/EU of 26 March 2013 (CELEX 32013D0162), which determines each EU Member State's annual greenhouse gas emission allocation for the years 2013 to 2020 under the Effort Sharing Decision (No 406/2009/EC). It exists to give a workspace with EU freight, ocean, road, or air exposure a single record of a background national climate-accounting instrument: this Decision allocates emission budgets to Member States, not to private freight-forwarding operators.

FACT: "COMMISSION DECISION of 26 March 2013 on determining Member States’ annual emission allocations for the period from 2013 to 2020 pursuant to Decision No 406/2009/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council (notified under document C(2013) 1708) (2013/162/EU)" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013D0162*

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "This Decision is addressed to the Member States.." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013D0162*

*Legal Confirmation Required:* This Decision is a Member-State-to-Member-State climate accounting instrument under the Effort Sharing Decision; the captured text states no duty running from a Member State, or from the Commission, to a private freight forwarder, carrier, or logistics operator. Its relevance to the workspace is contextual: it is one input into the national emission-reduction trajectories that shape a Member State's later, workspace-facing sectoral policy.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-13: the captured text is a 2013 Commission Decision covering the already-elapsed 2013 to 2020 period; it states no pending or future action item for a workspace reading it today.*

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "This Decision is addressed to the Member States.." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013D0162*

*Analytical inference:* because this Decision addresses obligations to Member States rather than private operators, the workspace's own compliance chain runs through whatever Member-State-level sectoral measure later implements the national emission-reduction trajectory this Decision quantifies, not through this Decision directly.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "should be defined by a linear trajectory starting with that member State’s average quantity of greenhouse gas emissions in the year 2009 and ending with its annual emission allocation for the year 2020." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013D0162*

*Per the workspace's reading:* this recital states the calculation method (a linear trajectory) underlying the year-by-year national allocation figures in Annexes I and II; it is Commission methodology, not a workspace-facing requirement.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

**1.** Event: 2013, compliance_deadline. FACT: "HAS ADOPTED THIS DECISION: Article 1 The annual emission allocations for each Member State for each year of the period from 2013 to 2020 are set out in Annex I and shall apply subject to any adjustments published pursuant to Article 10 of Decision No 406/2009/EC." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013D0162*

*Operational implication:* this is the first year of the eight-year allocation period; the captured text states the allocations for each subsequent year through 2020 are set out in Annex I, subject to Article 10 adjustments this brief's corpus does not itself carry the text of.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Decision create a compliance duty running to a private freight-forwarding operator?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. FACT: "This Decision is addressed to the Member States.." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013D0162* No source in this brief's corpus states an obligation running from this Decision to a freight forwarder, carrier, or logistics intermediary.

**Q2: Does a jurisdiction-specific trigger exist within this Decision?**

FACT: "Article 3 The annual emission allocations for Croatia as set out in Annex I shall apply as of the date of entry into force of the Treaty of Accession of Croatia." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013D0162*

*Analytical inference:* this is the only Member-State-specific trigger clause the captured text states; it is procedural (tying Croatia's own allocation figures to its accession-treaty entry into force) rather than a duty on a private party.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. Base annual emission allocations, 2013 to 2020 (Article 1).** FACT: "HAS ADOPTED THIS DECISION: Article 1 The annual emission allocations for each Member State for each year of the period from 2013 to 2020 are set out in Annex I and shall apply subject to any adjustments published pursuant to Article 10 of Decision No 406/2009/EC." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32013D0162*

**5. Period start (primary deadline).** FACT: the annual allocations described in obligation 1 above run "for each year of the period from 2013 to 2020" per Article 1's own text (quoted above); 2013 is the first year the allocation figures in Annex I apply.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Directive 2006/66/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 6 September 2006 on batteries and accumulators and waste batteries and accumulators (CELEX 32006L0066), repealing Directive 91/157/EEC. It exists to give a workspace that ships, handles, or forwards batteries and accumulators (or products incorporating them) a single record of the EU's placing-on-market prohibitions, collection and recycling targets, and compliance-calendar deadlines this Directive sets.

FACT: "Done at Strasbourg, 6 September 2006." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006L0066*

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Article 2 Scope 1. This Directive shall apply to all types of batteries and accumulators, regardless of their shape, volume, weight, material composition or use. It shall apply without prejudice to Directives 2000/53/EC and 2002/96/EC." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006L0066*

*Operational implication:* a workspace moving batteries or accumulators of any type, or appliances incorporating them, through the EU falls within this Directive's scope regardless of the battery's shape, volume, weight, or chemistry, subject only to the narrow exclusions in Section 12.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-13: this record-grade item's captured source is a 2006 Directive whose transposition and compliance-calendar dates (2007 to 2016) have all already elapsed; the captured text states no pending or future action item for a workspace reading it today.*

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "This Directive is addressed to the Member States.." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006L0066*

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this Directive is addressed to Member States, which transpose it into national law (Section 8, obligation 9); a workspace's direct compliance duty runs through the transposing national legislation of the Member State in which it places batteries on the market, not through this Directive's own text.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "Member States may exempt producers which, relative to the size of the national market place very small quantities of batteries or accumulators on the national market, from the requirements of Article 16(1), on the condition that this does not impede the proper functioning of the collection and recycling schemes set up on the basis of Articles 8 and 12." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006L0066*

*Per the workspace's reading:* this is the only producer-size-based relief the captured text states; it is a Member-State option (Member States "may" grant it), not a default the workspace can assume applies without confirming the relevant Member State has exercised it.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

**1.** Event: 26 September 2009, compliance_deadline. FACT: "Member States shall ensure that, no later than 26 September 2009: (a) producers or third parties set up schemes using best available techniques, in terms of the protection of health and the environment, to provide for the treatment and recycling of waste batteries and accumulators; and" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006L0066*

*Operational implication:* this is the deadline by which Member States had to ensure producers or third parties had treatment and recycling schemes in place for waste batteries and accumulators; a workspace auditing historical EU battery-waste compliance for this period should treat 26 September 2009 as the operative date, not this Directive's own 2006 adoption date.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Directive apply uniformly to every battery type?**

*Analytical inference:* No. FACT: "portable batteries or accumulators, including those incorporated into appliances, that contain more than 0,002 % of cadmium by weight." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006L0066* The cadmium prohibition applies specifically to portable batteries and accumulators (Section 8, obligation 2), while the mercury prohibition (obligation 1) applies to all batteries and accumulators; industrial and automotive batteries carry their own separate collection and disposal rules (Section 8).

**Q2: Does the workspace's own role (producer, distributor, or forwarder) change which obligations apply?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the captured text places most direct duties on "producers" (a person placing batteries on the market on a professional basis) and on Member States; whether a specific workspace role in a given battery shipment makes it a "producer" under this Directive's own definition is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. Mercury prohibition, all batteries.** FACT: "Member States shall prohibit the placing on the market of: (a) all batteries or accumulators, whether or not incorporated into appliances, that contain more than 0,0005 % of mercury by weight" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006L0066*

**2. Cadmium prohibition, portable batteries.** FACT: "portable batteries or accumulators, including those incorporated into appliances, that contain more than 0,002 % of cadmium by weight." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006L0066*

**3. Minimum collection rate targets.** FACT: "Member States shall achieve the following minimum collection rates: (a) 25 % by 26 September 2012; (b) 45 % by 26 September 2016." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006L0066*

**4. Treatment and recycling scheme deadline.** FACT: "Member States shall ensure that, no later than 26 September 2009: (a) producers or third parties set up schemes using best available techniques, in terms of the protection of health and the environment, to provide for the treatment and recycling of waste batteries and accumulators; and" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006L0066*

**5. Recycling efficiency deadline.** FACT: "Recycling processes shall, no later than 26 September 2010, meet the recycling efficiencies and associated provisions set out in Annex III, Part B." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006L0066*

**6. Battery-capacity labelling deadline.** FACT: "Member States shall ensure that the capacity of all portable and automotive batteries and accumulators is indicated on them in a visible, legible and indelible form by 26 September 2009." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006L0066*

**7. Producer registration.** FACT: "Member States shall ensure that each producer is registered." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006L0066*

**8. Small producer exemption.** FACT: "Member States may exempt producers which, relative to the size of the national market place very small quantities of batteries or accumulators on the national market, from the requirements of Article 16(1), on the condition that this does not impede the proper functioning of the collection and recycling schemes set up on the basis of Articles 8 and 12." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006L0066*

**9. National transposition deadline.** FACT: "Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive by 26 September 2008." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006L0066*

*Operational implication:* obligations 1 through 8 above only bind a workspace once transposed into the national law of the relevant Member State; 26 September 2008 was the deadline for that transposition to occur.

**10. Penalties.** FACT: "Member States shall lay down rules on penalties applicable to infringements of national provisions adopted pursuant to this Directive and shall take all necessary measures to ensure that they are implemented. The penalties provided for must be effective, proportionate and dissuasive. Member States shall notify those measures to the Commission by 26 September 2008." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006L0066*

**11. Entry into force.** FACT: "This Directive shall enter into force on the day of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006L0066*

**12. Addressee.** FACT: "This Directive is addressed to the Member States.." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006L0066*

**13. Scope.** FACT: "Article 2 Scope 1. This Directive shall apply to all types of batteries and accumulators, regardless of their shape, volume, weight, material composition or use. It shall apply without prejudice to Directives 2000/53/EC and 2002/96/EC." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006L0066*

No phase-in beyond the fixed compliance-calendar dates already stated in obligations 3 through 6 above is stated in Articles 1 to 30.

Obligations surveyed: 13; workspace-adjacent: 11; extracted as FACT: 13.

Shortfall: obligations 12 (Addressee) and 13 (Scope) are foundational/definitional rather than workspace-facing duties in their own right; they are captured to state who this Directive binds and what it covers, not to add a further compliance date.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

FACT: "Member States shall prohibit the placing on the market of: (a) all batteries or accumulators, whether or not incorporated into appliances, that contain more than 0,0005 % of mercury by weight" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006L0066*

*Analytical inference:* a workspace's product-specific compliance status turns on which battery category (portable, industrial, or automotive) and which substance threshold (mercury, cadmium) a given battery falls under; this brief's corpus does not itself carry a per-product classification for any specific workspace shipment.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "Member States shall ensure that each producer is registered." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006L0066*

*Operational implication:* registration is a producer-level, Member-State-administered requirement (Section 8, obligation 7); a workspace acting purely as a forwarder or distributor, rather than as the entity placing batteries on the market for the first time, would not itself be the registrant.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Operational implication:* a workspace tracking EU battery compliance should record 26 September 2008 (transposition and penalty-notification deadline), 26 September 2009 (treatment/recycling scheme and labelling-capacity deadline), 26 September 2010 (recycling efficiency deadline), 26 September 2012 (25% collection target), and 26 September 2016 (45% collection target) as the fixed compliance-calendar dates this Directive sets, all already elapsed as of this brief's own capture.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "Member States may exempt producers which, relative to the size of the national market place very small quantities of batteries or accumulators on the national market, from the requirements of Article 16(1), on the condition that this does not impede the proper functioning of the collection and recycling schemes set up on the basis of Articles 8 and 12." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006L0066*

*Analytical inference:* this small-producer exemption from the Article 16(1) financing obligation is the captured text's own genuine exception; it is discretionary to each Member State, not automatic.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-13: the captured text is confined to the Directive itself (recitals, articles, and annexes); it states no adjacent industry research or alternative scheme.*

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

FACT: "Done at Strasbourg, 6 September 2006." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006L0066*

- 6 September 2006: Directive 2006/66/EC adopted at Strasbourg.
- 26 September 2008: national transposition deadline; also the Article 25 penalty-notification deadline and Directive 91/157/EEC's repeal effective date.
- 26 September 2009: treatment/recycling scheme deadline (Article 12(1)) and battery-capacity labelling deadline (Article 21(2)).
- 26 September 2010: recycling efficiency deadline (Article 12(4)).
- 26 September 2012: 25% minimum collection rate target (Article 10(2)(a)).
- 26 September 2016: 45% minimum collection rate target (Article 10(2)(b)).

*Source for timeline entries: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32006L0066*

# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Implementing Decision 2012/134/EU of 28 February 2012 (CELEX 32012D0134), establishing the best available techniques (BAT) conclusions under Directive 2010/75/EU (the Industrial Emissions Directive) for the manufacture of glass. It exists to give a workspace with EU glass-manufacturing installations in its supply chain, or handling glass-industry cargo, a single record of the BAT-conclusions permitting reference this Decision sets.

FACT: "Done at Brussels, 28 February 2012." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012D0134*

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "SCOPE These BAT conclusions concern the industrial activities specified in Annex I to Directive 2010/75/EU, namely: — 3.3. Manufacture of glass including glass fibre with a melting capacity exceeding 20 tonnes per day; — 3.4. Melting mineral substances including the production of mineral fibres with a melting capacity exceeding 20 tonnes per day. These BAT conclusions do not address the following activities: — Production of water glass, covered by the reference document Large Volume Inorganic Chemicals – Solids and Other Industry (LVIC-S) — Production of polycrystalline wool — Production of mirrors, covered by the reference document Surface Treatment Using Organic Solvents (STS)" *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32012D0134*

*Operational implication:* only glass and mineral-fibre melting installations with a melting capacity exceeding 20 tonnes per day fall within these BAT conclusions; smaller installations, and the three named excluded activities (water glass, polycrystalline wool, mirror production), are outside their scope.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks a bilateral international agreement, not a rulemaking with private-party compliance duties: the AGREEMENT between the European Union and its Member States, of the one part, and Iceland, of the other part, concerning Iceland's participation in the joint fulfilment of the commitments of the European Union, its Member States and Iceland for the second commitment period of the Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change. It exists to give a workspace with EU or Icelandic exposure a single place to see what obligations this Agreement creates between the Union, its Member States, and Iceland, and what (if anything) that chain implies for a private freight-forwarding operator.

FACT: establishing the second commitment period of the Kyoto Protocol from 1 January 2013 until 31 December 2020. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22015A0804(02)

*Analytical inference:* the obligations described throughout this document run between sovereign parties (the Union, its Member States, and Iceland) under the Kyoto Protocol; this Agreement itself creates no duty running to a private freight-forwarding operator.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This Agreement is a treaty implementing the Kyoto Protocol's second commitment period (2013 to 2020) for the Union, its Member States, and Iceland; it is not itself an emissions-trading, reporting, or product regulation that a freight forwarder complies with directly.

FACT: the application of Article 3(1) of the Kyoto Protocol to greenhouse gas emissions from aviation and shipping for the Member States and Iceland is based on the Convention's approach of only including emissions from domestic flights and domestic shipping in Parties' targets. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22015A0804(02)

*Operational implication:* a workspace operating international air or ocean freight through the Union or Iceland should read this fact narrowly: this Agreement's own national Kyoto accounting excludes international flights and shipping from the Parties' targets, so it does not itself capture a freight forwarder's international transport emissions. Instruments that do address aviation and maritime emissions directly (for example the EU Emissions Trading System's aviation and maritime provisions) sit outside this Agreement's own text and outside this brief's corpus.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No content for this section.* This Agreement's own reporting and ratification deadlines (Section 8) have already elapsed as of this record's own capture; the captured source states no action item currently open for a private freight-forwarding workspace.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* This Agreement's compliance chain runs between the Union, its Member States, and Iceland as Parties to the Kyoto Protocol; it does not run to a private freight forwarder. Whether any Union or Icelandic measure implementing this Agreement's terms (for example national legislation applying Regulation (EU) No 525/2013 in Iceland) ever creates a reporting duty flowing down to a private operator is a fact-specific question outside this brief's scope and requires counsel review on the specific measure.

FACT: This Agreement shall be ratified by the Parties in accordance with their respective national requirements. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22015A0804(02)

*Analytical inference:* ratification and entry into force (Section 8) are procedural steps between the Parties; they do not themselves create or activate any duty running to a freight-forwarding workspace.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: The joint statement issued in Doha on 8 December 2012 states that the quantified emission limitation and reduction commitments for the Union, its Member States, Croatia and Iceland for the second commitment period under the Kyoto Protocol are based on the understanding that those commitments will be fulfilled jointly in accordance with Article 4 of the Kyoto Protocol. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22015A0804(02)

*Per the workspace's reading:* the Doha joint statement is the political predicate for this Agreement; the Agreement itself (Articles 1 to 11 and Annexes 1 and 2) is the operative instrument this brief grounds against, not the joint statement alone.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

1. Compliance deadline, 15 April 2015 (event kind: compliance deadline, now elapsed): Iceland was required, verbatim, "Iceland shall, by 15 April 2015, submit to the Secretariat of the UNFCCC a report to facilitate the calculation of its assigned amount, in accordance with this Agreement, the requirements of the Kyoto Protocol, the Doha Amendment and decisions adopted thereunder." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22015A0804(02)

*Analytical inference:* this deadline is a historical export entry from this item's own forward-events record; it has already passed as of this record's own capture and is retained here as the record's own dated obligation, not as a pending action item.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Agreement create direct regulatory obligations on private freight-forwarding operators?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. Every obligation identified in this Agreement's own text (Section 8) runs between the Union, its Member States, and Iceland as Parties to the Kyoto Protocol. Whether any Union or Icelandic implementing measure ever creates a downstream duty on a private operator is a separate, fact-specific question requiring counsel review.

**Q2: Does this Agreement's aviation and shipping scope exclusion mean international freight emissions are unregulated?**

*Analytical inference:* No. Section 8's aviation/shipping fact states only that this particular Kyoto joint-fulfilment Agreement's own national targets exclude domestic and, by the Convention's approach described in that fact, international flights and shipping from the Parties' assigned amounts. It says nothing about whether a separate instrument (outside this brief's corpus) regulates those emissions.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this is a bilateral international agreement implementing the Kyoto Protocol, not a binding regulatory instrument addressed to private parties. "Substantive requirements" here means the Agreement's own stated obligations on the Union, its Member States, and Iceland (the Parties bound by the Kyoto Protocol) plus the operational implications those obligations carry for a freight forwarder as an observer of the resulting EU/Iceland climate-treaty architecture.*

**1. Joint fulfilment of quantified emission commitments.** FACT: The Parties agree to fulfil their quantified emission limitation and reduction commitments for the second commitment period inscribed in the third column of Annex B to the Kyoto Protocol jointly, in accordance with the terms of the joint fulfilment. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22015A0804(02)

**2. Iceland's individual assigned-amount ceiling.** FACT: Iceland shall take all necessary measures in order to ensure that its aggregate anthropogenic carbon dioxide equivalent emissions in the second commitment period of the greenhouse gases listed in Annex A to the Kyoto Protocol from sources and sinks covered by the Kyoto Protocol, which do not fall under the scope of the ETS Directive, do not exceed its assigned amount set out in the terms of the joint fulfilment. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22015A0804(02)

*Operational implication:* this obligation is the mechanism by which ETS-covered emissions are excluded from Iceland's own Kyoto ceiling to avoid double counting; a workspace whose Icelandic operations fall under the EU Emissions Trading System scheme is accounted for there, not under this Agreement's own national ceiling.

**3. Application of Union legal acts to Iceland (jurisdictional scope).** FACT: The legal acts listed in Annex 1 of this Agreement shall be binding upon Iceland and rendered applicable in Iceland. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22015A0804(02)

*Operational implication:* Annex 1's own list (Regulation (EU) No 525/2013 on monitoring and reporting of greenhouse gas emissions, and current and future delegated/implementing acts under it) is the actual scope of Union law this Agreement extends into Iceland; a workspace tracking EU climate-reporting architecture in Iceland should treat Regulation 525/2013 as the relevant instrument, not this Agreement's own text.

**4. Iceland's UNFCCC reporting obligation (primary deadline).** FACT: Iceland shall, by 15 April 2015, submit to the Secretariat of the UNFCCC a report to facilitate the calculation of its assigned amount, in accordance with this Agreement, the requirements of the Kyoto Protocol, the Doha Amendment and decisions adopted thereunder. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22015A0804(02)

**5. The Union's own UNFCCC reporting obligation.** FACT: The Union shall prepare a report to facilitate the calculation of the assigned amount of the Union and a report to facilitate the calculation of the joint assigned amount of the Union, its Member States and Iceland (‘the joint assigned amount’), in accordance with this Agreement, the requirements of the Kyoto Protocol, the Doha Amendment and decisions adopted thereunder. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22015A0804(02)

**6. Breach-notification obligation.** FACT: Iceland shall notify the Joint Fulfilment Committee of any failure or impending failure to apply the provisions of this Agreement. Any such failure must be justified to the satisfaction of its members within 30 days of its notification. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22015A0804(02)

**7. Consequence of a breach (penalty summary).** FACT: Iceland shall account for the aggregate anthropogenic carbon dioxide equivalent emissions from sources and removals by sinks in Iceland covered by the Kyoto Protocol in the second commitment period, including emissions from sources covered by the European Union scheme for greenhouse gas emission allowance trading, against its quantified emission reduction objective included in the third column of Annex B of the Kyoto Protocol and, at the end of the second commitment period, retire from its national registry AAUs, CERs, ERUs, RMUs, tCERs or lCERs equivalent to those emissions. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22015A0804(02)

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this consequence is an emissions-accounting and unit-retirement obligation running to Iceland as a Party, not a fine, penalty, or enforcement action against any private freight operator. No source in this brief's corpus states a compliance deadline, fine, or penalty running to a freight forwarder, carrier, or logistics intermediary under this Agreement.

**8. Annex 1 exception (Regulation 525/2013 not fully applied to Iceland).** FACT: this Agreement's own Annex 1 states, verbatim, that Regulation (EU) No 525/2013 is applied to Iceland "except for its Articles 4, 7 lit. f, 15 to 20 and 22", with Article 21's provisions applying "as relevant." *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22015A0804(02)

**9. Aviation and shipping scope exclusion.** FACT: the application of Article 3(1) of the Kyoto Protocol to greenhouse gas emissions from aviation and shipping for the Member States and Iceland is based on the Convention's approach of only including emissions from domestic flights and domestic shipping in Parties' targets. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22015A0804(02)

**10. Entry into force (effective date).** FACT: This Agreement shall enter into force on the ninetieth day after the date on which all Parties have deposited their instrument of ratification. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22015A0804(02)

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 11 of this Agreement. Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above (obligation 8, the Annex 1 exception for Regulation 525/2013's Articles 4, 7 lit. f, 15 to 20 and 22). Scope limits: No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 11 of this Agreement.

Obligations surveyed: 12; workspace-adjacent: 3; extracted as FACT: 10.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section.* This Agreement addresses national greenhouse-gas accounting between the Union, its Member States, and Iceland; the captured source states no product-specific compliance status of any kind.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: Iceland shall, by 15 April 2015, submit to the Secretariat of the UNFCCC a report to facilitate the calculation of its assigned amount, in accordance with this Agreement, the requirements of the Kyoto Protocol, the Doha Amendment and decisions adopted thereunder. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22015A0804(02)

FACT: The Union shall prepare a report to facilitate the calculation of the assigned amount of the Union and a report to facilitate the calculation of the joint assigned amount of the Union, its Member States and Iceland (‘the joint assigned amount’), in accordance with this Agreement, the requirements of the Kyoto Protocol, the Doha Amendment and decisions adopted thereunder. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22015A0804(02)

*Operational implication:* both reporting obligations run state-to-UNFCCC-Secretariat (Iceland's own report and the Union's own report); there is no registration or reporting mechanism in this Agreement's own text through which a private freight-forwarding operator registers or reports.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*No content for this section.* This Agreement's own text describes no technical, monitoring, or reporting system a freight-forwarding workspace would need to operate; its Joint Fulfilment Committee (Article 6) is a governance body of the Parties themselves, not a system a private operator interacts with.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: No reservations may be made to this Agreement. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:22015A0804(02)

*Analytical inference:* the Agreement's own bar on reservations means no Party (including Iceland) may unilaterally exempt itself from any of this Agreement's terms; this is a governance rule between the Parties and creates no exemption pathway for a private freight-forwarding operator.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section.* This Agreement's own text names no adjacent industry body, coalition, or alternative-compliance research program; the captured source is limited to the Agreement and its two Annexes.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 8 December 2012: the joint statement setting the political basis for this Agreement's joint-fulfilment commitments was issued in Doha.

# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/656, which amends Annex II (technical
specifications) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 (the Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation) as regards
standards for wireless recharging, electric road system, vehicle-to-grid communication and hydrogen supply
for road transport vehicles. It exists to give a workspace tracking EU electric-vehicle and hydrogen
infrastructure standards a single place to see which standards apply, from which dates, and to which
vehicle categories.

FACT: Done at Brussels, 2 April 2025. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R0656

*Analytical inference:* the source's own header states its Official Journal publication date as "18.6.2025" (18 June 2025, day.month.year); Article 2's own twenty-day entry-into-force rule (Section 8) runs from that date.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This is a Commission delegated act amending technical standards, not a new obligation on freight forwarders
directly. Its duty-holders are original equipment manufacturers, recharging- and refuelling-point operators,
and Member States; a freight-forwarding workspace is affected only to the extent it operates, procures, or
advises on EV recharging or hydrogen refuelling infrastructure.

FACT: The amendments to the titles and scope of points 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 of Annex II to Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 are necessary to achieve a clearer presentation of the standards applicable for each vehicle category. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R0656

*Operational implication:* the underlying Annex II points are each scoped to a specific vehicle category
(light-duty electric vehicles, L-category electric vehicles, electric buses, heavy-duty electric vehicles);
a workspace should match its own vehicle fleet or infrastructure to the correct point before relying on any
single obligation below.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: It shall apply from 8 January 2026. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R0656

*Operational implication:* 8 January 2026 is the general application date; recharging points installed or
renovated on or after that date must meet the updated standards (Section 8), while points installed before
that date may continue under the prior standard until renovated.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* This Regulation's duties run to original equipment manufacturers and
recharging/refuelling point operators (Section 8); it states no duty running to a freight forwarder that
neither manufactures vehicles nor operates recharging or refuelling infrastructure. Whether a workspace
that operates recharging points at its own facilities (for an EV fleet, for example) falls within scope of
a specific Annex II point is a fact-specific question requiring counsel review against the workspace's own
equipment.

FACT: This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R0656

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: The Commission may amend Annex II on technical specifications of Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 to introduce new technical specifications or update references to the standards set out in that Annex. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R0656

*Per the workspace's reading:* this recital states the Commission's own delegated-act authority under
Article 21(3) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1804; this Regulation is that authority's exercise, not a standalone
instrument.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section.* The item's own export carries no forward_events rows; every dated
milestone this record grounds is already confirmed in the captured text and is carried in Section 14.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Regulation create a direct compliance duty on a freight forwarder that does not manufacture
vehicles or operate recharging/refuelling infrastructure?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No duty of that kind is stated in the captured text. Every obligation in
Section 8 runs to original equipment manufacturers, recharging- or refuelling-point operators, or Member
States.

**Q2: Does the L-category vehicle scope language (Section 8) mean other vehicle categories are unregulated?**

*Analytical inference:* No. The jurisdictional-scope fact in Section 8 states only that Annex II point 1.3
(as retitled by this Regulation) applies to L-category electric vehicles; separate Annex II points (1.1,
1.2, 1.4, 1.6) cover light-duty vehicles, electric buses, and heavy-duty vehicles respectively, each with
its own standards.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this delegated act's obligations run to original equipment manufacturers, recharging- and
refuelling-point operators, and Member States (the Commission's own stated duty-holders), not to a private
freight-forwarding operator directly. "Substantive requirements" here means the Regulation's own stated
technical standards and dates, plus the operational implications those carry for a workspace that operates,
procures, or advises on EV or hydrogen infrastructure.*

**1. Entry into force.** FACT: This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R0656

**2. General application date (primary deadline).** FACT: It shall apply from 8 January 2026. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R0656

**3. Binding and directly applicable in all Member States.** FACT: This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R0656

**4. Jurisdictional scope: L-category electric vehicles.** FACT: The title of point 1.3 should also be changed to clarify that in the context of Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 it applies to L-category electric vehicles only. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R0656

**5. Titles-and-scope clarification across Annex II points 1.1 to 1.3.** FACT: The amendments to the titles and scope of points 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 of Annex II to Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 are necessary to achieve a clearer presentation of the standards applicable for each vehicle category. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R0656

**6. AC normal-power recharging points for light-duty electric vehicles (point 1.1).** FACT: alternating current (AC) normal-power recharging points for light-duty electric vehicles installed or renovated from 8 January 2026 shall be equipped, for interoperability purposes, at least with socket-outlets or vehicle connectors of Type 2 for Mode 3 recharging as described in standard EN IEC 62196-2:2022 or, if their power is less than or equal to 3,7 kW and their primary purpose is the recharging of electric vehicles in Mode 2, with socket-outlets compliant with standard IEC 60884-1:2022 *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R0656

*Operational implication:* a workspace deploying or procuring AC normal-power recharging points for
light-duty EVs at its own facilities must specify the correct connector standard depending on the
installation date (8 January 2026) relative to the point's own install/renovation date.

**7. Vehicle-to-grid communication standard, publicly accessible points, from 1 January 2027 (recital).** FACT: the publicly accessible recharging points for the vehicle-to-grid communication interface for road vehicles installed or renovated from 1 January 2027 should at least also comply with standard part EN ISO 15118-20:2022 *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R0656

**8. Vehicle-to-grid communication standard, publicly accessible points, from 1 January 2027 (Annex II point 2.1.2, operative text).** FACT: Publicly accessible recharging points for alternating current (AC) and direct current (DC) for light- and heavy-duty electric vehicles installed or renovated from 1 January 2027 shall comply, for interoperability purposes, at least with standard EN ISO 15118-20:2022 *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R0656

**9. Commission's own delegated-act authority (basis for this Regulation).** FACT: The Commission may amend Annex II on technical specifications of Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 to introduce new technical specifications or update references to the standards set out in that Annex. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R0656

**10. Complementary relationship with NIS2 cybersecurity requirements.** FACT: As Directive (EU) 2022/2555 includes operators of recharging points as part of a sector of high criticality, the application of that Directive and the requirements set out in Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 should be complementary. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R0656

*Operational implication:* a workspace that itself operates recharging points is, per this recital, within
Directive (EU) 2022/2555's sector of high criticality for cybersecurity purposes; that Directive's own
requirements are outside this brief's captured pool.

**11. Exemption for existing low-level-communication recharging points (edge case, developed further in Section 12).** FACT: existing publicly accessible recharging points for Mode 3 and 4 recharging using low-level communication such as PWM, which are already capable of communicating with electric vehicles on the market equipped with EN ISO 15118-2:2016, should be exempted from implementing Parts 1 to 5 of standard EN ISO 15118 or subsequent extended versions like EN ISO 15118-20:2022. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R0656

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED (see metadata.requirement_trajectory: adopted 2 April 2025, general application and updated connector/V2G-communication standards from 8 January 2026, next-generation vehicle-to-grid standard EN ISO 15118-20:2022 mandatory from 1 January 2027). Exceptions and carve-outs: No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 and 2 of this Regulation (the exemption described above for existing low-level-communication recharging points is stated in a recital discussing the Annex, not in either of this Regulation's two Articles). Scope limits: CAPTURED above (obligation 5, the titles-and-scope clarification across Annex II points 1.1 to 1.3).

Obligations surveyed: 15; workspace-adjacent: 5; extracted as FACT: 11.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

FACT: alternating current (AC) normal-power recharging points for light-duty electric vehicles installed or renovated from 8 January 2026 shall be equipped, for interoperability purposes, at least with socket-outlets or vehicle connectors of Type 2 for Mode 3 recharging as described in standard EN IEC 62196-2:2022 or, if their power is less than or equal to 3,7 kW and their primary purpose is the recharging of electric vehicles in Mode 2, with socket-outlets compliant with standard IEC 60884-1:2022 *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R0656

*Operational implication:* the same install/renovation-date logic (Section 8, obligation 6) applies across
every Annex II point this Regulation touches (normal-power, high-power, L-category, bus, heavy-duty, and
wireless recharging points, plus hydrogen refuelling connectors): a workspace should check the specific
point number against its own equipment's install or renovation date before assuming a given standard
applies.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

*No content for this section.* The captured text states no registration or reporting mechanism through
which a private freight-forwarding operator registers or reports under this Regulation.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*No content for this section.* This Regulation's own technical standards (Section 8) are connector and
communication-protocol specifications for recharging- and refuelling-point hardware; the captured text
states no operational system requirement addressed to a freight-forwarding workspace as such.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: existing publicly accessible recharging points for Mode 3 and 4 recharging using low-level communication such as PWM, which are already capable of communicating with electric vehicles on the market equipped with EN ISO 15118-2:2016, should be exempted from implementing Parts 1 to 5 of standard EN ISO 15118 or subsequent extended versions like EN ISO 15118-20:2022. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R0656

*Analytical inference:* this exemption is scoped to EXISTING publicly accessible recharging points already
using low-level communication (such as PWM) that can already talk to vehicles equipped with EN ISO
15118-2:2016; it does not exempt newly installed or renovated recharging points, which must meet the
updated standards from the dates stated in Section 8.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section.* The captured text names no adjacent industry body or alternative-compliance
research program beyond the European standardisation organisations (CEN and Cenelec) that developed the
standards this Regulation adopts, which are not themselves an alternative compliance pathway.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 2 April 2025: this Regulation was adopted, verbatim, "Done at Brussels, 2 April 2025."
- 18 June 2025: this Regulation's Official Journal publication date, stated in the source's own header as "18.6.2025" (18 June 2025).
- 8 January 2026: general application date; updated recharging-point connector and vehicle-to-grid
  communication standards apply to newly installed or renovated points from this date.
- 1 January 2027: standard part EN ISO 15118-20:2022 becomes mandatory (in addition to EN ISO 15118-2:2016)
  for newly installed or renovated publicly accessible recharging points, and covers private recharging
  points for Mode 3 or Mode 4 recharging from this date too.

*Source for timeline entries: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32025R0656*

*Operational implication:* the two dated milestones above (8 January 2026, 1 January 2027) are the two
compliance-relevant dates a workspace tracking this Regulation's own connector and communication standards
needs on its calendar.
