# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks a UK Statutory Instrument, The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment)
Regulations 2013 (S.I. 2013/1037), which amends the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme Regulations
2012 to implement a temporary EU derogation from aviation-emissions monitoring, reporting, and surrender
obligations that arose before 2013.

FACT: These Regulations implement Decision No 377/2013/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 24 April 2013 derogating temporarily from Directive 2003/87/EC establishing a scheme for greenhouse gas emission allowance trading within the Community. *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1037

*Analytical inference:* this instrument's own purpose is narrow and conditional: it relieves a defined
class of aircraft operators (those who return certain 2012 aviation allowances) from civil-penalty exposure
for a specific pre-2013 compliance window; it does not remove the underlying monitoring, reporting, or
surrender duties themselves for operators who do not meet that condition.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This instrument amends aviation-emissions-trading obligations under the UK's implementation of the EU
Emissions Trading Scheme. It applies directly to aircraft operators (a class that can include a
freight-forwarding workspace operating or chartering air cargo flights) with monitoring, reporting, or
allowance-surrender duties arising from aviation activity in 2010, 2011, or 2012.

FACT: which came into force on 1st January 2013 *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1037

*Operational implication:* a workspace with UK-connected air cargo operations from before 2013 should
confirm whether it held any duty under regulations 20, 21, or 26 of the 2010 Regulations (monitoring,
reporting, or surrender) and, if so, whether the conditional relief in Section 8 applied to it.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No content for this section.* Every deadline this instrument's own text states (31 March 2013, 29 April
2013, 30 April 2013, 3 May 2013, 23 May 2013, 29 May 2013) has already elapsed as of this record's own
capture; the captured source states no currently open action item.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* This instrument's duties and conditional relief run to "aircraft operators"
and to "P" (any person on whom a duty is imposed under regulations 20, 21, or 26 of the 2010 Regulations),
per its own regulation 87A. Whether a specific freight-forwarding workspace held aircraft-operator status
for aviation emissions purposes in 2010-2012 is a fact-specific question requiring counsel review against
that workspace's own historical flight operations.

FACT: penalty in respect of a failure to— (a) monitor aviation emissions, contrary to regulation 20 of the 2010 Regulations *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1037

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: This instrument's own Explanatory Note states, verbatim: 'which came into force on 1st January 2013' (referring to the
Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme Regulations 2012, S.I. 2012/3038, which this instrument amends).
*Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1037

*Per the workspace's reading:* the 2012 Regulations are the operative UK implementing instrument this
amendment modifies; the 2010 Regulations (S.I. 2010/1996) were revoked by the 2012 Regulations but their
pre-2013 obligations and civil penalties are preserved by regulation 87 of the 2012 Regulations, per this
instrument's own Explanatory Note.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section.* The item's own export carries no forward_events rows; every dated milestone
this record grounds is a past, elapsed date, carried in Section 14.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this instrument create a NEW civil-penalty exposure for aircraft operators?**

*Analytical inference:* No. It creates a conditional RELIEF from an existing civil-penalty exposure
(Section 8) that already applied under regulation 87 of the 2012 Regulations for pre-2013 aviation
emissions; it does not itself create a new duty or a new penalty.

**Q2: Does the jurisdictional-scope fact (Section 8) mean flights within the EEA are unaffected by this
instrument?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* The captured text states the derogation applies to flights to or from an
aerodrome OUTSIDE the EEA (with named exceptions for closely connected areas); whether a specific flight
pattern falls inside or outside that boundary is a fact-specific question requiring counsel review against
the workspace's own route network.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this instrument's own duty-holders are "aircraft operators" and, within regulation 87A, the defined
person "P"; a freight-forwarding workspace is a duty-holder only to the extent it held aircraft-operator
status for aviation emissions purposes in 2010-2012.*

**1. Entry into force.** FACT: These Regulations may be cited as the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Regulations 2013 and come into force on 23rd May 2013. *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1037

**2. Definitional amendment exception (regulation 3).** FACT: (and, except in regulation 87A(3), “allocated” has the corresponding meaning) *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1037

**3. Underlying reporting duty (regulation 21, 2010 Regulations).** FACT: Under regulation 21, an aircraft operator must (for each calendar year from 1st January 2010) submit to the regulator a verified report of aviation emissions, and must do so by 31st March in the following year. *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1037

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this duty is preserved by regulation 87 of the 2012 Regulations, not created
by this amending instrument; this instrument's own contribution is the conditional relief at obligation 8
below.

**4. 31 March 2013 reporting deadline preserved.** FACT: Those obligations are accordingly preserved up to and including the 31st March 2013 reporting deadline. *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1037

**5. Underlying surrender duty (regulation 26, 2010 Regulations) (primary deadline).** FACT: Under regulation 26, the aircraft operator must (for each calendar year from 1st January 2012) surrender emissions trading allowances, or project credits under the Kyoto Protocol, equal to the operator’s aviation emissions in that year, and must do so by 30th April in the following year. *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1037

**6. 30 April 2013 surrender deadline preserved.** FACT: That obligation is accordingly preserved for the purpose of the 30th April 2013 surrender deadline. *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1037

**7. Civil penalty for failing to monitor (penalty summary).** FACT: Furthermore, the civil penalty for failing to monitor aviation emissions in each of the calendar years 2010, 2011 and 2012 continues to apply. *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1037

**8. Conditional relief from civil penalty.** FACT: penalty in respect of a failure to— (a) monitor aviation emissions, contrary to regulation 20 of the 2010 Regulations. *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1037

*Operational implication:* relief from this penalty is conditional (obligation 9 below), not automatic; an
aircraft operator that does not meet the condition remains exposed to the penalty described in obligation 7.

**9. Condition for relief: return international allowances by 29 May 2013.** FACT: has, before 29th May 2013, returned a sum of aviation allowances allocated for 2012 equal to the international allowances that were issued to P. *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1037

**10. Jurisdictional scope of the EU derogation.** FACT: The EU Decision requires Member States not to enforce those obligations for the years in question, to the extent that they arise in respect of flights to or from an aerodrome outside the European Economic Area (EEA), unless the aerodrome is in a closely connected area (such as Switzerland, Croatia, or a dependent territory of an EEA state). *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1037

**11. Scope limit: derogation does not apply if free allocation retained.** FACT: However, that temporary derogation does not apply where the aircraft operator has (for 2012) been issued with a free allocation of aviation allowances in respect of such flights, and has not returned an equivalent number of such allowances. *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1037

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED (see metadata.requirement_trajectory: the
2010-2012 underlying duties, the 2012 Regulations' 1 January 2013 entry into force, and this instrument's
own 2013 dates from 29 April 2013 through 29 May 2013). Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED above
(obligation 2, the "except in regulation 87A(3)" definitional carve-out). Scope limits: CAPTURED above
(obligation 11, "that temporary derogation does not apply where...").

Obligations surveyed: 13; workspace-adjacent: 8; extracted as FACT: 10.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section.* This instrument addresses aviation-emissions monitoring, reporting, and
allowance-surrender duties; the captured text states no product-specific compliance status.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: Under regulation 21, an aircraft operator must (for each calendar year from 1st January 2010) submit to the regulator a verified report of aviation emissions, and must do so by 31st March in the following year. *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1037

FACT: Those obligations are accordingly preserved up to and including the 31st March 2013 reporting deadline. *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1037

*Operational implication:* the annual verified-emissions-report obligation (regulation 21, 2010
Regulations) is the reporting mechanism this instrument's own Explanatory Note describes; this amending
instrument does not itself add a new reporting channel.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*No content for this section.* The captured text describes a registry mechanism (the Union Registry
"aviation return account") operated by the registry administrator for cancelling returned allowances; it
states no operational system requirement addressed to a freight-forwarding workspace as such.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: However, that temporary derogation does not apply where the aircraft operator has (for 2012) been issued with a free allocation of aviation allowances in respect of such flights, and has not returned an equivalent number of such allowances. *Source: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1037

*Analytical inference:* this edge case turns on whether the aircraft operator both received a free 2012
allocation AND failed to return an equivalent number of allowances; meeting either half of that test alone
does not disqualify an operator from the relief described in Section 8.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section.* The captured text names no adjacent industry body or alternative-compliance
research program; it is limited to this instrument and its own Explanatory Note.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 1 January 2010: underlying aviation-emissions monitoring, reporting, and surrender duties under the 2010
  Regulations begin to accrue for each calendar year from this date.
- 1 January 2013: the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme Regulations 2012 (S.I. 2012/3038), which
  revoked and replaced the 2010 Regulations with savings and transitional provisions, came into force,
  verbatim, "which came into force on 1st January 2013"
- 31 March 2013: the preserved annual aviation-emissions reporting deadline for pre-2013 emissions.
- 29 April 2013: this amending instrument was made, verbatim, "Made 29th April 2013"
- 30 April 2013: the preserved annual allowance-surrender deadline for pre-2013 emissions.
- 3 May 2013: this amending instrument was laid before Parliament, verbatim, "Laid before Parliament 3rd May 2013"
- 23 May 2013: this amending instrument comes into force.
- 29 May 2013: the deadline for an aircraft operator to return international allowances to qualify for the
  conditional civil-penalty relief in Section 8.

*Source for timeline entries: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1037*

# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Commission Regulation (EU) No 900/2014, which amends Regulation (EC) No 440/2008
(the test-methods regulation under REACH, Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006) to add six new OECD-derived test
methods for chemical toxicity and eco-toxicity assessment. It exists to give a workspace handling
REACH-regulated chemical substances a single place to see what this update changed and when it took
effect; it is NOT itself a compliance obligation running to a freight-forwarding operator, because its own
duty-holders are REACH substance registrants and the testing laboratories that generate their dossier data.

FACT: Regulation (EC) No 440/2008 'contains the test methods for the purposes of the determination of the physico-chemical properties, toxicity and eco-toxicity of chemicals to be applied for the purposes of Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006.' *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0900

*Analytical inference:* this Regulation amends that test-methods framework; it does not itself impose a
registration, reporting, or labelling duty on a freight forwarder that neither registers chemical
substances nor operates a testing laboratory.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

This is a technical amending Regulation adding laboratory test methods to the REACH test-methods
framework. Its content is overwhelmingly a scientific Annex of OECD-style test-method protocols (animal
husbandry, dosing, and observation procedures for six new toxicity studies); it applies to a
freight-forwarding workspace only as background awareness of the current test-methods edition, should a
client or upstream shipper ask about the currency of REACH dossier data.

FACT: It is necessary to update Regulation (EC) No 440/2008 to include with priority new and updated test methods recently adopted by the OECD in order to take into account technical progress, and to ensure the reduction of the number of animals to be used for experimental purposes, in accordance with Directive 2010/63/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0900

*Operational implication:* a workspace should treat this Regulation as background regulatory-currency
awareness for REACH-regulated chemical cargo, not as a source of its own compliance duties.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*No content for this section.* This Regulation's own entry-into-force date (three days after its 21 August
2014 Official Journal publication) has long since elapsed as of this record's own capture; the captured
source states no currently open action item.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* This Regulation's own text names no duty running to a freight-forwarding
operator; its duty-holders are REACH substance registrants (who must use the updated test methods to
generate dossier data) and the testing laboratories that conduct the studies described in the Annex.
Whether a specific workspace's own REACH obligations (as an importer, downstream user, or registrant in its
own right) are affected by this test-methods update is a fact-specific question requiring counsel review
against the workspace's own REACH role.

FACT: The Annex to Regulation (EC) No 440/2008 is amended in accordance with the Annex to this Regulation. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0900

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: Regulation (EC) No 440/2008 'contains the test methods for the purposes of the determination of the physico-chemical properties, toxicity and eco-toxicity of chemicals to be applied for the purposes of Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006.' *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0900

FACT: The measures provided for in this Regulation are in accordance with the opinion of the Committee established under Article 133 of Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0900

*Per the workspace's reading:* this Regulation was adopted through the REACH Committee comitology
procedure under Article 133 of Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006, the same procedure that governs other REACH
implementing measures.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*No content for this section.* The item's own export carries no forward_events rows; every dated milestone
this record grounds is a past, elapsed date, carried in Section 14.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Regulation create a compliance duty running to a freight forwarder?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No duty of that kind is stated in the captured text. Every obligation in
Section 8 runs to REACH substance registrants or to the testing laboratories that conduct the described
studies, not to a freight-forwarding operator as such.

**Q2: Is the deep scientific Annex content (animal husbandry and dosing procedures) itself a regulatory
obligation the workspace must track?**

*Analytical inference:* No. That content is laboratory test-conduct methodology (how a testing laboratory
must run a given OECD-derived study), not a business compliance obligation; it is surveyed and represented
in Section 8 only as illustrative examples of what this amendment's technical content consists of, not as a
duty running to this platform's own customer base.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this Regulation's own duty-holders are REACH substance registrants and testing laboratories, not
freight-forwarding operators. The pool for this item is 383,612 characters, but roughly 380,000 of those
characters are a single homogeneous class of content -- OECD-style laboratory test-method protocol
instructions (animal husbandry, dosing regimens, and observation schedules across six new toxicity study
types) -- rather than distinct legal obligations. This section therefore surveys the Regulation's own
operative Articles and recitals in full, plus a small representative sample of the Annex's protocol-level
facts (the required primary_deadline/jurisdictional_scope slots, one exception, and one scope statement)
rather than individually enumerating every one of the Annex's dozens of similarly-shaped procedural
instructions, which would misrepresent workspace relevance rather than clarify it.*

**1. Entry into force.** FACT: This Regulation shall enter into force on the third day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0900

**2. Binding and directly applicable in all Member States.** FACT: This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States. *Source: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014R0900
